core: Explicit int(), float(), str(), and bool() conversion
Suitable numeric strings and predictable ValueError

claims.claim: int(), float(), str(), and bool() are built-in type constructors whose calls can explicitly create values of their target types.
int('42') returns an integer, while int('6.25') raises ValueError because decimal text is not an integer literal.
float('6.25') returns a float, while unsuitable numeric text such as 'not-a-number' raises ValueError.
str(19) creates the string '19', and str(7.0) creates '7.0'.
bool('') is False and bool('False') is True because the latter string is nonempty.
bool is a subclass of int, although Boolean values are conventionally used to represent truth values.
